notes: Background: SMB product company building a docs-first help center and internal knowledge base with smart answer summarization.
Primary push: replace keyword search with embeddings + reranking to reduce 'no answer' hits and surface authoritative passages.
Documents: ~500k small docs (support articles, transcripts), average 300 tokens per doc; expect to ingest gradually over 3 months.
Traffic profile: early stage — ~20k queries/month expected in Q2, spiky during campaigns. Target p99 latency for user-facing answers < 500ms, median < 200ms if possible.
Cost sensitivity: high. They want clear per-embedding cost estimates and recommendations on dimensionality (512 vs 1536) to balance accuracy vs cost.
Model preference: prefer open models for embeddings and a smaller open generation model for reranking. Interested in quantized variants to reduce cost.

Vector DB: customer currently evaluating Pinecone and Weaviate; asked how Redwood hosted API integrates (connector vs SDK examples) and whether Redwood supports direct rerank endpoint to avoid double hop.

Integration questions raised in call: 1) batching best practices for bulk embedding ingestion, 2) recommended embedding dimensionality for their use-case, 3) how to do hybrid search + rerank with minimal latency, 4) SDK examples in Node + Python, 5) caching strategies for top-k rerank results.

Security: SMB but customer handles moderate private data; wants SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs for API usage, retention controls for uploaded docs. Asked whether Redwood hosted stores embeddings in a shared multi-tenant store or per-customer isolation.
Quote from CTO: "We want self-serve to be legit — if we can POC in two weeks and see cost predictability, we can convert. Avoiding vendor lock-in for vectors is a plus."
Current status: exploratory proof-of-concept. Has run small tests but needs SE help to scale ingestion and a short bench comparing response times vs Pinecone for their topology.
Attached artifacts: pricing deck requested (drive link above), sample ingestion spreadsheet, small set of anonymized transcripts used for initial tests.

Requested deliverables: short checklist for production ingestion, a 15-20 minute bench note comparing Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank vs embedding->third-party vector DB round trip (latency + cost), security FAQ for SOC2 items.
Notes on billing: they are on trial credits; want to know predictable buckets (embeddings per 1M, generations per token) and recommendations on rate limits to avoid surprise charges.
Next practical step: schedule a 60-minute SE workshop to walk through their ingestion pipeline (CSV -> chunking -> embed batch) and run small bench. Avery to propose times for week of 2026-03-15.
